lessons.hypothesis: agents can sign commits with any identity
lessons.lesson: Agents must never invent identity data (emails/usernames) without explicit human authorization.
lessons.context: First agent commit used fake emails (*@scire.local); the human rejected and the keys were regenerated without email. verified via 2026-09-06-foundation-identity.md.

lessons.lesson: Setup must merge existing config, never overwrite: preserve plugin/mcp/keys; use {env:VAR} instead of plaintext.
lessons.context: setup.js re-wrote opencode.json dropping plugins/MCPs and injected OMNIROUTE_API_KEY in plaintext (never reached git). verified via 2026-09-06-infra-fixes-grader-setup-agents.md.

lessons.lesson: Validate tool/config schemas against the runtime docs before fixing formats; mark [UNVERIFIED] otherwise.
lessons.context: Agents assumed tools:/permissions: frontmatter; correct key is permission:. OpenCode would not load the agents. verified via 2026-09-06-infra-fixes-grader-setup-agents.md.

lessons.lesson: State the metric's direction (higher/lower-is-better) before running the grader; the default flips the verdict.
lessons.context: accuracy 0.9 vs baseline 0.8 without --higher-is-better reads as -12.50% and would FAIL. Ran with the flag and PASSed. verified via 2026-09-06-exp-hello-smoke-test.md.

lessons.hypothesis: spawnSync runs npm .cmd bins on Windows
lessons.lesson: On Windows, spawnSync does not run .cmd bins without shell:true (or cmd.exe /d /s /c quoting); handle .cmd explicitly.
lessons.context: CLI bin scire failed with ENOENT resolving .cmd; fixed by spawning cmd.exe with windowsVerbatimArguments. verified by reproduction (npm ENOENT), 2026-09-07-smoke-test-cli-scire.md.

lessons.lesson: Honor a user's tool preference but detect already-installed alternatives; do not download a large dep when a working one exists.
lessons.context: User preferred TinyTeX but MiKTeX 25.12 already present; setup used the existing pdflatex instead of forcing a ~150MB download. 2026-09-07-smoke-test-cli-scire.md.

lessons.hypothesis: fancy glyphs render reliably on Windows console
lessons.lesson: Keep mascot/UI art mostly plain ASCII for Windows console reliability; require a font check before introducing rare glyphs.
lessons.context: Rebuilt SCIRE owl in src/cli/owl.mjs with ASCII and fractional 24-bit ANSI; Unicode (◉★) avoided deliberately. 2026-09-07-ui-redesign-owl-hermes.md.

lessons.lesson: For agentic safety evaluation, judge from state artifacts (receipts, final-state snapshots, canary tokens, tool-call traces) rather than transcript/LLM-reasoning alone; state-grounded judges report 7.73-11.72 pp higher ASR than trajectory judges.
lessons.context: REDAgentBench (arXiv:2608.10669) 1661 cases, 6 models x 3 harnesses, McNemar p<=6.54e-5. Prior SCIRE lesson 'declare-metric-direction-before-grading' is the same discipline at a smaller scale.

lessons.hypothesis: state-grounded evaluation equals deterministic invariant checking
lessons.lesson: Do not conflate 'state-grounded evaluation' (an LLM judge fed receipts/DB snapshots, e.g. REDAgentBench State Judge) with 'deterministic invariant checking' (TrustHarness MustCall/ForbidCall/NoCanaryLeak). They have different reliability and cost; coverage claims must be measured per class, not assumed.
lessons.context: Evaluator shock-test of H6 brief: the brief's '80% coverage' and '<2% marginal LLM value' figures were [UNVERIFIED] estimates presented with excess confidence. Verified via evaluation 2026-09-08-H6-deterministic-rule-first-judging-evaluation.md.

lessons.hypothesis: estimating coverage thresholds is acceptable in a hypothesis
lessons.lesson: Coverage thresholds (e.g. 'invariants cover >=80% of high-severity failures') are empirical claims that must be measured, not estimated; flag invented thresholds [UNVERIFIED] and design the experiment to falsify them (H6-1, H6-2).
lessons.context: Evaluator rejected the unmotivated 80% and <2% thresholds in the H6 brief. Lesson reinforces anti-hallucination ladder Tier 0: [UNVERIFIED] flag before presenting estimates as findings.

lessons.hypothesis: deterministic invariants always dominate LLM judges
lessons.lesson: The efficacy delta between deterministic invariant checking and LLM judging is not a single number but type-dependent: deterministic gates dominate on observable-trace harms (tool misuse, canary leak, approval bypass) where they achieve near-zero leak (NetInjectBench 0/240 <=1.58% vs LLM judge 10%), but are structurally blind to semantic-intent harms. The crossover point must be measured per harm class, not assumed.
lessons.context: ED-2 evaluator SUPPORT: the (a)-observable / (b)-semantic classification from trajectory-judge (arXiv:2609.00038) and NetInjectBench (arXiv:2607.10490) corrects the H6 evaluator's core concern about invented thresholds.

lessons.hypothesis: deterministic gating alone determines safety efficacy
lessons.lesson: The largest measured efficacy delta is not deterministic-vs-LLM per se but whether the checker is grounded in trusted, non-artifact state (metadata, policy, canonical action objects) versus operating on untrusted text. A metadata-aware policy gate achieves 0/240 unsafe actions while preserving 99.17%+ usefulness; static allowlisting (rigid, non-adapted grounding) achieves 0% usefulness / 100% overblock on the same corpus. The quality of the grounding policy is the decisive variable.
lessons.context: ED-3 evaluator SUPPORT: NetInjectBench (arXiv:2607.10490) direct comparison; CAVA (arXiv:2607.13716) canonicalization substrate. The engineering implication: invest in grounding quality (policy specification, canonical actions) rather than just choosing deterministic vs LLM.

lessons.hypothesis: a deterministic gate achieves >=77% silent-fault recall (matching the LLM step-judge)
lessons.lesson: The step-rubric LLM judge's 77% silent-fault recall (trajectory-judge arXiv:2609.00038) is an LLM performance baseline, NOT a deterministic-gate achievement. No study has measured deterministic-gate recall on the same fault-injected corpus. Hypotheses must not import LLM judge performance as the target for deterministic systems — the two have different failure modes. Silent faults may be precisely the category where deterministic gates underperform because the observable trace appears normal.
lessons.context: ED-1 evaluator CHALLENGE: the brief imported the 77% step-judge number as a deterministic gate target. Required modification: reframe as 'measure deterministic gate recall independently' rather than claiming it matches the LLM step-judge.
